Empirical Research Plan  
“Does banking competition foster firm‐level innovation?  Evidence from the staggered intrastate branching deregulations, 1976–2006”

---------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
---------------------------------------------------------
Strategy:  Staggered Difference-in-Differences (DID) complemented with an event-study.  

Why appropriate  
• Treatment (intrastate branching deregulation) occurred in different years across states for plausibly idiosyncratic political‐economy reasons → classic staggered policy shock.  
• Outcomes (patents, citations, R&D) are observed annually for firms that can be mapped to a state.  
• We want the average causal effect of greater banking competition on innovation relative to the counterfactual path absent deregulation.  

Implementation details  
• Use modern DID estimators that are unbiased under staggered adoption and heterogeneous effects:  
  – Callaway–Sant’Anna (2021) group-time ATT, or  
  – Sun–Abraham (2021) interaction-weighted estimator.  
• Use an event-study (relative-time leads & lags) to probe pre-trends and dynamics, estimated by demeaning within cohort × calendar-year cells or by SA2021’s ‘eventstudy’ routine.  

---------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control
---------------------------------------------------------
Treatment variable  
D_it = 1 if firm i’s headquarters state s has deregulated intrastate branching by year t, 0 otherwise.  Stays =1 thereafter (absorbing).

Control group  
In year t the control group is all firms in states that have not yet deregulated.  (If any states never deregulate they provide “always-controls.”)

Treatment timing / event date  
adopt_s = year in which state s enacted intrastate branching deregulation (Kroszner–Strahan series, updated to 2010).  Event time τ = t – adopt_s.

Firms are stacked into cohorts by adopt_s.  For the event-study we omit τ = −1 as the baseline.

---------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
---------------------------------------------------------
A1. Parallel trends:  In the absence of deregulation, patent outcomes of treated and not-yet-treated firms would have followed parallel paths (after conditioning on firm & year fixed effects and covariates).  
Plausibility:  Reasonable—timing driven by within-state politics rather than technology cycles.  Will be probed with pre-trend tests and state-specific time trends.

A2. No anticipation:  Firms do not change innovation before the law is passed (or do so only in the year of passage, which we can drop).  
Plausibility:  Most laws passed quickly after legislative agreement; anticipation window likely short.  Leads in event-study will test.

A3. Stable treatment & no partial compliance:  Once branching is allowed, it is not withdrawn.  All firms in the state face the new banking structure.  
Plausibility:  True—no state reversed deregulation.

A4. SUTVA / no cross-state spillovers:  A state’s deregulation does not directly affect firms headquartered in other states.  
Plausibility:  Some cross-border lending occurred, but intrastate rules chiefly changed in-state branch expansion.  Will test by excluding border-county HQs.

A5. Composition stability:  No selective migration of innovative firms into treated states right after deregulation.  
Plausibility:  Headquarters moves are rare; we will check firm attrition and run balanced-panel robustness.

---------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification and Mitigation
---------------------------------------------------------
Threat 1:  Other state policies correlated with deregulation (e.g., R&D tax credits, interstate banking later on).  
Mitigation:  Control for observable contemporaneous policies; include state × year covariates (e.g., corporate tax rate, R&D tax credit dummies); include separate indicator for interstate branching (post-1994).

Threat 2:  Differential macro shocks (oil boom, IT boom) hitting certain states contemporaneously with deregulation.  
Mitigation:  State-specific linear and quadratic trends; region-year fixed effects; industry × year fixed effects (industry defined at 3-digit SIC).

Threat 3:  Treatment effect heterogeneity biases TWFE.  
Mitigation:  Use C&S or SA estimators, report cohort-specific ATTs, aggregate using appropriate weights; also run stacked DID (Baker et al. 2022) as robustness.

---------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline
---------------------------------------------------------
```r
#---------------------------------------------------
# 0.  Packages
#---------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)      # fast manipulation
library(fixest)          # fast fe regressions
library(did)             # Callaway–Sant’Anna DID
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)

#---------------------------------------------------
# 1.  Load data
#---------------------------------------------------
pat   <- fread("patents_firm_year.csv")      # firm_id, year, patents, cites
comp  <- fread("compustat_firm_year.csv")    # R&D, assets, leverage etc.
reg   <- fread("branch_dereg_dates.csv")     # state, adopt_year
bank  <- fread("bank_hhi_state_year.csv")    # HHI, branches

#---------------------------------------------------
# 2.  Merge & construct variables
#---------------------------------------------------
dt <- merge(pat, comp, by=c("firm_id","year"))
dt <- merge(dt, bank, by=c("state","year"), all.x=TRUE)
dt <- merge(dt, reg,  by="state", all.x=TRUE)

# Treatment indicators
dt[, adopt_year := adopt_year]                         # from reg
dt[, treat := as.integer(year >= adopt_year)]
dt[, rel_year := year - adopt_year]                    # event time
dt[, never := is.na(adopt_year)]                       # never-treated flag
dt[, gname := ifelse(never, 9999, adopt_year)]         # group = cohort

# Winsorize patents
dt[, patents := pmin(patents, 200)]

#---------------------------------------------------
# 3.  Main specification (firm & year FE)
#---------------------------------------------------
est_main <- feols(patents ~ treat + RnD + log(assets) + leverage |
                  firm_id + year, data=dt)
summary(est_main, cluster = ~state)

#---------------------------------------------------
# 4.  Callaway–Sant’Anna DID
#---------------------------------------------------
cs <- att_gt(yname="patents",
             gname="gname",
             idname="firm_id",
             tname="year",
             xformla = ~ RnD + log(assets) + leverage,
             data = dt[!never])          # exclude never if desired
agg_effects <- aggte(cs, type="dynamic")  # event study
summary(agg_effects)
ggdid(agg_effects)                        # plot leads/lags

#---------------------------------------------------
# 5.  Robustness:  drop border HQ states
#---------------------------------------------------
border_states <- c("NY","NJ","PA","IL", ...)  # define manually
est_rob <- feols(patents ~ treat |
                 firm_id + year, data=dt[!state %in% border_states])
summary(est_rob, cluster=~state)
```

---------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results
---------------------------------------------------------
Economic intuition:  Banking competition lowers borrowing costs, especially for smaller or more opaque firms, thereby relaxing financial constraints that impede R&D.  Expect:  
• Positive impact on patent counts (≈ 5–10 % increase over five years post-dereg.)  
• Larger impact on forward citations (quality) and on firms with ex-ante high leverage or low internal cash.  

---------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)
---------------------------------------------------------
C1: No systematic pre-trend differences ………………… 0.8  
C2: No anticipation of treatment …………………………… 0.7  
C3: No contemporaneous confounding policies ………… 0.6  
C4: Stable treatment and SUTVA …………………………… 0.9  
C5: Correct estimator for staggered adoption ………… 1.0  

(1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable/absent.  Average = 0.8)
